title: Night prayer
tomorrow: why does Adam have a job before anything goes wrong?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the evening examen: thanks first, then the day hour by hour. The line was where was God. Now, the last prayer before sleep.

Two in the morning, and the brain won't stop: tomorrow's shift, the thing you said, the text you never answered. Handing the day over is hard. Luke tells about someone who did it in the worst hour there is. Midafternoon, outside Jerusalem. The sun's light fails, Luke says, and darkness covers the land. The veil of the Temple is torn down the middle. And Jesus, dying on the cross, cries out with a loud voice.
screen: `TWO IN THE MORNING.` → `DARKNESS OVER THE LAND.` → `A LOUD VOICE.`

segments.voice: What he says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit." Those are his last words in Luke. And they weren't new. They come from a psalm, Psalm 30 in the Douay numbering: "Into thy hands I commend my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, the God of truth." He dies praying a line from the prayer book of his people. To commend is to hand something over for safekeeping, the way you'd leave what matters most with someone you trust. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: the Church's Night Prayer, called Compline, puts that same line in its short response before sleep. So people who pray it end each day with Jesus's last words in Luke. Sleep, in that light, is a small rehearsal of trust. Nobody can stay awake guarding everything. Night Prayer admits it and hands it over: the order you got wrong, the fight that isn't fixed, the people you love. Psalm 4, one of the psalms of Night Prayer, ends with someone lying down in peace to sleep and rest.
screen: `FATHER, INTO THY HANDS.` · `A LINE FROM A PSALM.` · `COMPLINE, EVERY NIGHT.` · `SLEEP AS TRUST.` · then, large: `INTO THY HANDS.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and open your hands on your lap, palms up. Let three things from today rest in them, one at a time, and hand each one over with the Compline line, into thy hands; if prayer isn't yours, let a slow breath out carry each one off.
Night prayer. Compline, the Church's last prayer of the day, with Jesus's last words in Luke at its heart.
Hold onto this: into thy hands, the whole day handed over before sleep. Good night.

howItsDone: Night Prayer (Compline) is the last hour of the Liturgy of the Hours; it includes a brief examination of conscience, a psalm, the responsory 'Into your hands, Lord,' and Simeon's canticle, and many lay Catholics pray it before bed.
